name: Maasai
overview: Maasai is a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as the son of Adiel. His mention in Scripture is brief and focused, with no additional notes or broader narrative provided. He stands as a representative figure within the Levitical lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Maasai means 'work of YHWH,' indicating a connection to the Lord's service or activity. This proper name underscores a possible dedication to God's work, although it was not explicitly given by God according to the record in 1 Chronicles 9:12.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Maasai as the son of Adiel, establishing his direct paternal lineage. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented for Maasai.
scriptureSignificance: Maasai's significance lies in his association with the Levitical tribe, known for their sacred duties in Israel. As the son of Adiel, he is part of the genealogical record that preserves the heritage of those who served in the temple and upheld the worship of God. His mention in 1 Chronicles 9:12 situates him within the faithful remnant dedicated to God's work, reflecting the ongoing importance of Levitical service in the biblical narrative.
